We want toget goodstories told.

There's a gap between the skills it takes to write a captivating story and the skills it takes to run an effective querying campaign.

That gap is where good stories go to die.

So let's bridge it.

How will we do it?

Illustration · The paper avalanche
01

Take the admin off your plate.

Querying throws off a surprising amount of detail. Who you sent to, which pages they asked for, when they said they'd reply. Most of us keep it in a spreadsheet that gets harder to read with every row. QueryHawk keeps it for you, and shows you where every query stands at a glance.

Illustration · Reading the signs
02

Show you what's working.

Thirty queries in, it's hard to tell whether your letter is the problem or you've just been unlucky. QueryHawk keeps count as you go: which version of your letter drew requests, which opening pages got read on. It won't pretend a handful of replies is a pattern. It will show you what they say so far.

Illustration · Minding the shop
03

Mind our own business.

Your manuscript, your agent list and your rejections belong to you. We won't sell them, show you adverts, or use anything you write to train AI. And we won't try to write for you: no generated query letters, no rewrites of your pages. QueryHawk does the admin, because that's what it's good at. The writing is yours.

Illustration · The founder's desk

A note from the founder

Hello, I'm Nick.

I started querying with a spreadsheet, like most people do. I work with spreadsheets for a living, and it still got away from me. Which version of the letter went to whom, which agent had said no reply means no, which nudge was already a week late.

So I built the tool I wanted. QueryHawk is designed, built and run by me, here in the UK, while I query a manuscript of my own. I use it every day, so I find the rough edges fast.

And if you write in, it's me who answers. .

Nick

Nick PhysickFounder
